AMC pointed to the various new EPA regulations which will be in effect in MY 1979. AMC cited the Senate-House conference report indicating that the problem of individual manufacturers should be a severe strain on a manufacturer.

AMC claimed that the original proposal of 18.7 mpg would be a severe strain on them.
AMC commented that they agreed with NHTSA in not setting standards for NPA's of greater than 6000 pounds GVWR.
With regard to setting a higher or lower standard,

AMC stated they can meet only 17 mpg in MY 1979 with their

Jeep CJ vehicles, exclusive of emission standard and

test procedure effects. They pointed out that NHTSA can

set standards for separate classes of NPA's and stated

that a separate class should be established for their

Jeep CJ vehicle if they are included under the Act (a point

they contest in their comments to the NPRM).
